title: Bistable by Construction: Wall-Clock-Calibrated State Monitors Have No Moment-Detection Regime at Agent Cadence
abstract: arXiv:2606.19386v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Runtime monitors for autonomous agents commonly threshold an accumulated internal state - a behavioural baseline, a drift statistic, or, in our prior work, a modelled affective state. We previously reported a State Saturation Trap: threshold-on-state triggers over a continuous affect engine become near-constant alarms on SWE-bench debugging agents (Modgil 2026). A post-release audit found the engine received dt=0 between actions, so its exponential decay never operated: the published trap is a pure-accumulator result. We correct the record (erratum, v2) and treat the flaw as an experiment. The key variable it exposes is whether a monitor's dynamics are calibrated in sample time (per observation, as in CUSUM) or wall-clock time (half-lives in seconds, as in affect models and EMA baselines). On fixed-rate streams these coincide; on agent streams, where inter-action time varies by orders of magnitude, they do not. A pre-registered

translated_title: 构造性双稳态：以墙钟时间校准的状态监测器在智能体节奏下不存在瞬时检测机制
translated_abstract: 面向自主智能体的运行时监测器通常对累积的内部状态设定阈值——可以是行为基线、漂移统计量，或在我们先前工作中的建模情感状态。我们曾报告过一种“状态饱和陷阱”：在连续情感引擎之上基于状态阈值的触发机制，会在 SWE-bench 调试智能体上变成近乎持续不断的报警（Modgil 2026）。发布后的审计发现，该引擎在动作之间接收到的 dt=0，因此其指数衰减从未运行：先前发表的陷阱实际上是一个纯累加器的结果。我们更正了记录（勘误，v2），并将这一缺陷视为一次实验。它所揭示的关键变量是：监测器的动态是以采样时间（按每次观测，如 CUSUM）校准，还是以墙钟时间（以秒为单位的半衰期，如情感模型和 EMA 基线）校准。在固定速率的数据流上二者重合；而在动作间隔时间相差数个数量级的智能体数据流上，二者并不重合。一项预先注册的……
tldr: 本文勘误并重新审视了先前报告的“状态饱和陷阱”（实为动作间 dt=0 导致指数衰减从未运行的纯累加器结果），揭示出以采样时间校准与以墙钟时间校准的监测器动态在固定速率流上等价、但在动作间隔差异巨大的智能体流上根本不同，因此墙钟时间校准的状态监测器在智能体节奏下不存在瞬时检测机制。
en_tdlr: Correcting the previously reported "State Saturation Trap"—actually a pure-accumulator artifact caused by dt=0 between actions that prevented exponential decay—this paper shows that sample-time-calibrated and wall-clock-calibrated monitor dynamics coincide on fixed-rate streams but diverge on agent streams, leaving wall-clock-calibrated state monitors with no moment-detection regime at agent cadence.
